children: The Sensex ends 329.91 points, or 0.44 per cent, lower at 74,529.08, while the Nifty declines 85.30 points, or 0.36 per cent, to 23,329

Indian equity benchmarks snapped a four-session winning streak on Tuesday, with the Sensex falling 330 points and the Nifty closing below the 23,350 mark as selling in information technology (IT), public sector bank and oil and gas stocks weighed on the market.

The benchmarks began the session on a positive note, supported by favourable global cues, but the gains failed to sustain. The Nifty slipped to an intraday low of 23,285.75 as selling pressure intensified during the first half of the session.

A decline in Brent crude prices provided some support. Oil prices fell for a fifth consecutive session, with Brent slipping below USD 100 a barrel. However, the decline in energy prices was not enough to offset weakness across several heavyweight sectors.
The Sensex ended 329.91 points, or 0.44 per cent, lower at 74,529.08, while the Nifty declined 85.30 points, or 0.36 per cent, to 23,329.
The broader market also closed marginally lower, with the Nifty Midcap 100 and Nifty Smallcap 100 indices ending in the red.

Information technology stocks were among the biggest drags on the market, with the IT index falling nearly 1 per cent. The public sector bank, fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG), pharmaceutical and oil and gas indices each declined around 0.5 per cent.
In contrast, the media index gained 1 per cent, while the realty index rose 0.9 per cent.

Tata Consumer Products, Bajaj Finserv, Nestle, Bajaj Finance and Grasim Industries were among the biggest Nifty losers. Coal India, InterGlobe Aviation, Eternal, Titan Company and Dr Reddy's Laboratories were among the key gainers.
Among individual stocks, Meesho gained 9 per cent after UBS retained its ‘buy’ recommendation and raised its price target to Rs 260.
Sansera Engineering advanced 7 per cent after Goldman Sachs maintained its ‘buy’ rating and raised its target price to Rs 4,990.
Blue Star declined 2 per cent after Jefferies retained its ‘hold’ rating with a target price of Rs 1,635.
Unicommerce eSolutions gained 5 per cent after announcing a partnership with The Sleep Company.
Augmont Enterprises fell 4 per cent after reporting a 15.3 per cent decline in profit, while Lumino Industries dropped 4 per cent despite reporting a 32.4 per cent increase in profit.
Pine Labs rose nearly 5 per cent after 4.97 crore shares changed hands in a block deal.
Transrail Lighting, Pace Digitek Among Movers
Transrail Lighting surged 15 per cent after announcing plans to increase its conductor manufacturing capacity.
Pace Digitek gained 9 per cent after its subsidiary secured a Rs 488.46-crore order from NTPC GE Power Services.
Aequs rose nearly 5 per cent after its board announced that it would consider a proposal for a preferential issue of warrants.
